$comment: Golden fixture manifest — specs/ai.md §9.1. One entry per image in images/.
Fields per §9.1: id, service, surface, deviceClass, captureNotes,
expectedTitleCount, expectedArtworkOnly, provenance. `file` is additive:
the corpus mixes .jpg/.png/.heic, so the extension is not derivable from
the id and a loader needs it explicitly (specs/ai.md §9.1 fixture tree).
expectedTitleCount is ground truth about the IMAGE, established by reading
it. It is never derived from model output — see specs/ai.md §9.4 and the
expected/ answer key, which carry the same rule. A count generated from a
reader's response would grade that reader against itself.
CROSS-IMAGE STRUCTURE — deliberate, and not a defect to be tidied away:
1. netflix-mylist-mobile-01 and -02 are two overlapping screenshots of
ONE scrolling list. Six of the eight titles on page 2 also appear on
page 1; the union is 10 distinct works. This is the real-world
deduplication case the product exists to handle (one row per title),
captured rather than constructed. Do NOT 'fix' the duplication.
2. netflix-mylist-desktop-01 holds exactly that union — the same 10
works, the same day, rendered ARTWORK ONLY with no captions. The
corpus therefore contains a controlled A/B: identical works, one
rendering with text and one without. Artwork-only recall (RSK-021)
can be measured against a text-verified ground truth rather than
against a visual identification alone.
3. netflix-artwork-only-01 is a LATER snapshot of the same Netflix list
and shares only 6 of its 10 works with the group above. It is the
clean-screenshot control for the Netflix desktop surface (the two
.heic slots are monitor photographs). Its differing membership is
the passage of time, not an inconsistency.
4. max-saved-mobile-01 and max-saved-desktop-01 are the same 6 works on
both Max surfaces. Both render text captions — the measured finding
of TASK-011 (docs/evaluation/capture-surfaces.md) that only Netflix
desktop renders artwork only.

images.captureNotes: Netflix iOS app, My List, sorted by 'Top Matches'. Page 1 of 2 of one scrolling list; see $comment note 1. Titles render as text captions beneath artwork. The eighth title ('Louis C.K.: Ridiculous') is partly occluded by the floating bottom navigation bar — a reader that drops it is failing on occlusion, not on text rendering. Heavy chrome: 'My List', 'TV Shows & Movies', 'Games', 'TV Shows', 'Movies', 'Haven't Started', 'Started', 'Sort By', 'Top Matches', 'Recently Added', 'Live', 'Monday', 'TOP 10', 'Home', 'Clips', 'Search', 'My Netflix'. 'Stranger Things: VHS Special Edition' WRAPS to two lines rather than truncating — no real capture in this corpus contains an ellipsis, which is why truncated-titles-01 is synthetic.

Netflix iOS app, My List. Page 2 of 2 of the same scrolling list as netflix-mylist-mobile-01, scrolled down; six of these eight titles also appear on page 1. Sort chips are scrolled out of view. See $comment note 1 — the overlap is the point.

PHOTOGRAPH OF A MONITOR, not a screenshot — carries bezel, glare down the left third, keystone distortion and a visible mouse cursor. A recall miss here must be diagnosed as capture quality before it is attributed to the reader; the clean-screenshot control for this same surface is netflix-artwork-only-01. Netflix web renders NO caption text — every title must be inferred from artwork alone (RSK-021). Holds exactly the union of netflix-mylist-mobile-01 and -02, so its ground truth is text-verified; see $comment note 2. Chrome is text and legible: 'Home', 'Shows', 'Movies', 'Games', 'New & Popular', 'My List', 'Browse by Languages'. 'Raw' additionally carries burnt-in artwork badges 'TOP 10', 'Live', 'Monday'; 'Wicked: For Good' carries 'Recently Added'.

Chrome-heavy negative case. This is the CONTINUE WATCHING rail, NOT a saved list — a reader may legitimately extract the single work, but the pipeline must not treat this surface as a My List capture. Heading reads 'Continue Watching for Let's Go!', which renders the owner's Netflix PROFILE NAME; retained deliberately with the owner informed (RSK-014). Single artwork-only tile with no caption.

HBO Max iOS app, My Stuff > My List. Titles render as text captions with a release year beneath. FALSE-POSITIVE TRAP: a 'Recommended For You' rail of partially visible tiles sits below the saved list; those are NOT saved titles and must not be extracted. Chrome: 'My Stuff', 'My List', 'Continue Watching', 'My Purchases', 'Recommended For You', 'New'.

PHOTOGRAPH OF A MONITOR, not a screenshot — bezel, glare across the top-left, keystone distortion, visible mouse cursor. Diagnose recall misses as capture quality first. Max web DOES render text captions with release years, which is why expectedArtworkOnly is false on a desktop surface; only Netflix desktop renders artwork alone (docs/evaluation/capture-surfaces.md). Same 6 works as max-saved-mobile-01. Carries the same 'Recommended For You' false-positive rail.

The RSK-021 headline case (specs/ai.md §9.4) and the clean-screenshot control for the Netflix desktop surface. A true screenshot, so no bezel, glare or cursor confound — a miss here is the reader, not the capture. NO caption text: all 10 works must be inferred from artwork alone. expectedTitleCount is the real number of works in the image (10), NOT zero; see the warning in §9.4 and do not 'correct' it back. A LATER snapshot of the same list than the mobile/desktop group, sharing only 6 works with it; see $comment note 3.

Drives the low-yield path. 'Genuinely contentless' means ZERO TITLES, not zero pixels: the image renders a full empty-state screen with chrome ('My List', 'Search', 'You haven't added anything yet.', 'Titles you add to your list will appear here.', 'Home', 'New & Hot', 'My List'). A pixel-blank rectangle would be passed by any implementation including one that returns [] unconditionally; chrome-with-no-titles discriminates, and any candidate produced from it is a real fabrication rather than a fixture defect.

Ellipsised captions — the specs/ai.md R2.3b case. SYNTHETIC BY NECESSITY, not by convenience: no real capture in this corpus truncates. The longest observed real caption, 'Stranger Things: VHS Special Edition', WRAPS to a second line instead (see netflix-mylist-mobile-01). The four captions are cut mid-word with a trailing ellipsis so that resolution must recover the full work from a prefix.

Compression-robustness case: netflix-mylist-mobile-01 resized to 640px wide and re-encoded at JPEG quality 18, so captions carry heavy ringing and blocking. Ground truth is identical to its source by construction — the same 8 titles, including the nav-bar-occluded eighth. A recall drop between this image and its source is attributable to compression alone, which is the measurement.

Orientation case: max-saved-mobile-01 rotated 90 degrees, with the rotation baked into the PIXELS and no EXIF orientation tag to undo it (all fixture metadata is stripped). A reader that relies on an orientation hint rather than on the image will fail here. Ground truth is identical to its source by construction — the same 6 titles, and the same 'Recommended For You' false-positive rail.
